Action Plan:
1. Provide symptomatic management for presumed gastroenteritis: advise clear fluids, start oral re-hydration solution (Dioralyte, OTC), continue paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) for pain/fever, and follow a soft diet (e.g., soup, mashed foods) advancing as tolerated.
2. Counsel on red-flag / safety-netting: if diarrhoea or vomiting persist >48 h, if unable to keep fluids down, reduced urine output, worsening abdominal pain, or objective fever >38 °C, patient to phone back or attend urgent care/ED.
3. Lifestyle advice: avoid alcohol until recovery; maintain good hand hygiene to prevent household spread; consider temporary avoidance of dairy if it provokes vomiting.
4. Follow-up: scheduled telephone review or patient-initiated call in 48 h if not improving.
5. Documentation: Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint – Profuse watery diarrhoea for 3 days (started Mon/Tue); frequency almost hourly while awake.  
• Associated symptoms – Crampy mid-lower abdominal pain (colicky, ~6/10, precedes stool), nausea, occasional vomiting (triggered by milk), subjective fever (“burning up”), slightly decreased urine output. No blood in stool.  
• Triggers – Dairy worsens nausea/vomiting; no clear food/travel trigger identified. Brother has similar illness for 5 days.  
• Past medical history – None reported; otherwise fit and well.  
• Medications – Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) as needed. No regular prescriptions.  
• Allergies – No known drug allergies.  
• Family history – Father: Stage-III colon cancer. Brother: current similar diarrhoeal illness.  
• Social history – 27-year-old male; lives with mother & sister; office job (government) in London; social smoker (occasional); alcohol socially with periodic binges; frequently eats takeaway meals.  

Objective:
• Telehealth visit – No vitals or physical examination performed.  
• No laboratory or imaging studies performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute watery diarrhoea with abdominal cramps  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis (High likelihood; DDx item “Acute viral gastroenteritis (likely norovirus)” – High).  
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Acute bacterial gastroenteritis/food-borne infection (Medium) – high stool frequency, subjective fever, takeaway food habit.  
     • Secondary transient lactose intolerance (Low-Medium) – vomiting after milk.  
     • Inflammatory bowel disease (Low) – acute onset; absent blood/mucus.  
   - Investigations planned: None at this time; consider stool culture, FBC, U&E if no improvement or signs of dehydration at 48 h review.  
   - Treatment planned:  
     • Oral re-hydration solution (Dioralyte) OTC; maintain clear fluids.  
     • Soft diet progressing as tolerated; avoid dairy if precipitates vomiting.  
     • Paracetamol for fever/abdominal pain.  
     • Avoid alcohol; rest at home.  
   - Relevant referrals: Not indicated presently; advise urgent care/ED if red-flag symptoms or dehydration develop.

Quality checks:
• Missing/expected elements: No objective vitals, weight, physical abdominal exam, or hydration status documented; no medication dose/frequency recorded; immunisation status (incl. COVID-19) not discussed; stool culture not obtained.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; no major inaudible sections.
